sentences.text: Mesosutterella multiformis, the type species, is an obligately anaerobic, Gram-stain-negative, rod or coccoid-shaped bacterium isolated from faecal samples of a healthy Japanese woman and man.
It was proposed as a novel genus of the family Sutterellaceae, forming a distinct lineage between the genera Parasutterella and Sutterella.
Mesosutterella faecium was later described from swine faeces as an obligate anaerobe whose genome suggested a low-toxicity lipopolysaccharide.
A study reported that this strain prevented the inflammatory response in a dextran sulfate sodium-induced colitis model.
Mesosutterella porci was described among four novel taxa isolated from the intestine of pigs.
